_note: Shared ruleset of folder-prefix rules consumed by all four 'where does real user/app data live, vs. system/app noise' features: header-scan tiers 1/2, nested-archive discovery, the embedded sqlite/plist sweep, and the Media Browser's 'User Media' filter. See app/scan_rules.py. Paths are CANONICAL (Cellebrite-format, no 'private/var/' prefix) -- FfsAdapter.prefix_shortcut() is applied per-path at load time for a GrayKey case, so this one file covers both iOS acquisition tools. 'include': 1 = in scope for header-scan/zip-discovery/embedded-media; 0 = excluded (always a subfolder nested under some include=1 row above it). 'user_media': 'not_user_media' | 'user_media_only' | 'also_user_media' -- independent of 'include', consumed only by the Media Browser's own filter (see app/scan_rules.py's user_media_prefixes()).

Confirmed empirically 2026-10-10 against a real iOS17 archive, via real CONTENT inspection (not just magic-byte TYPE) -- the real bar is 'linkable to the user,' not merely 'parses as JSON/plist/database.' Many real-typed cache files are purely generic system/service config (bundled reference data, A/B-test bucket IDs, server bootstrap URLs, ML model binaries) with NO content difference from one device/account to another -- those stay excluded despite having a real type. Kept IN scope: GeoServices (a paired Apple Watch's own offline map cache -- device ownership evidence), com.apple.HomeKit (real home/accessory configuration), com.apple.findmy.fmipcore (the actual Find My device list), com.apple.chrono (widget snapshot renders reflecting the user's own configured widgets and their live state), com.apple.ctcategories.service (cached App Store lookups tied to specific apps the user viewed -- thin but real). See the excludes below for the many subfolders that DO have a real file type but no real user-linkage.
